content.title: Plan-to-Execution Proof | A Fixed Storyboard Strip Witnesses Material Construction
content.summary: Keep one complete storyboard strip static and readable while a separate live execution field advances through material preparation, transformation, forming, reveal, and completion in the same planned order. Let each stage leave a comparable visible state, then close with the finished object and the unchanged final plan cell together. This is new evidence for the existing persistent-plan-strip selector, not a duplicate selector.

quick_start.input_format: persistent readable plan strip + separate execution field + planned event order + at least three visible state changes + plan and finished state together
quick_start.recommended_input: The lower fifth shows a complete five-cell icon-only plan strip while the upper field contains an original white ceramic root chamber, a cobalt gel vial, and a moss tray. A narrow copper heater passes once along the seam to seal it; the same chamber turns into the moss tray with seam and gel still traceable. End with the finished root chamber, sealed seam, cobalt gel, moss tray, and the unchanged last plan icon visible together.
required_anchors: Establish one complete static plan strip and a separate live execution field at the opening.
Keep the plan strip unchanged and readable while every live state advances in its order.
Reserve one decisive reveal that verifies an internal or completed property.
End with the finished result and the unchanged terminal plan cell visible together.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Keep one complete storyboard strip static and readable while a separate live execution field advances through material preparation, transformation, forming, reveal, and completion in the same planned order. Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.

Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Keep one static nonverbal plan strip fully visible in a dedicated zone while a larger execution field changes above it. Advance the execution field in the plan's order through functionally distinct, irreversible states; never edit, reorder or replace the reference strip. Reserve one decisive reveal for the finished-state proof, then hold the actual result together with the unchanged terminal plan cell. The reusable mechanism is persistent-plan verification and ordered execution escalation, not the source chocolate, cake, marble, storyboard artwork, title, twelve-cell layout, utensils, garnish, render style or exact process.

invariants.rule: Establish one complete static plan strip and a separate live execution field at the opening.
invariants.purpose: Makes intended and actual states simultaneously comparable.
invariants.ablation_failure: Showing the plan only once turns it into an intro card.

invariants.rule: Keep the plan strip unchanged and readable while every live state advances in its order.
invariants.purpose: Preserves the plan as a stable verification artifact.
invariants.ablation_failure: Animating or reordering the plan destroys direct comparison.

invariants.rule: Use at least three functionally different execution states with visible irreversible progress.
invariants.purpose: Proves actual work instead of decorative cutting.
invariants.ablation_failure: Repeated close-ups without state change do not execute the plan.

invariants.rule: Reserve one decisive reveal that verifies an internal or completed property.
invariants.purpose: Turns the chain into a payoff rather than a list of operations.
invariants.ablation_failure: A generic beauty shot cannot prove the preceding process succeeded.

invariants.rule: End with the finished result and the unchanged terminal plan cell visible together.
invariants.ablation_failure: Cropping away the plan at the end abandons the verification mechanism.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source chocolate bars, cream, eggs, cocoa, vanilla, salt, gold leaf and exact ingredient arrangement
the source white marble, copper bowls, double boiler, spatula, ramekin, oven, white glove, spoon and dark plate
the source molten lava cake, raspberry garnish, cocoa dust, chocolate flow and exact food choreography
the source twelve-cell food storyboard artwork, CHOCOLATE SYMPHONY title, small labels, icons and fixed lower-strip design
the source glossy animated-food rendering, warm amber grade, shot timing, logo, creator identity and prompt wording
